And those who disbelieve say, denying the resurrection and wondering at it: ﴿Shall we direct you to a man who will tell you﴾ meaning Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿when you are completely torn apart﴾ that is, cut into pieces, scattered in every way, and turned to dust, ﴿that you will indeed be in a new creation﴾? That is, he tells you that you will be in a new creation.

﴿Has he invented a lie against Allah, or is there madness in him?﴾ The alif here is an interrogative alif (alif al-istifham, the interrogative particle) that has entered before the alif of connection (alif al-wasl, the initial alif that is pronounced only when a word begins a sentence), and for this reason the verb is in the accusative (nasb). They are saying: Does he invent a lie, or is there madness (junun) in him?

Allah the Exalted said, refuting them: ﴿Rather, those who do not believe in the Hereafter are in punishment and far error﴾ from the truth in this world.

﴿Have they not looked at what is before them and behind them of the heaven and the earth?﴾ so that they would know that wherever they are, My earth and My heaven encompass them, and they cannot escape from its regions, and I am Able to act against them. ﴿If We will, We shall cause the earth to swallow them﴾ Al-Kisa'i recited, "nakhsif bihim" (We shall cause to swallow them), with idgham (assimilation, merging of one consonant into the next) of the fa' into the ba'. ﴿Or We shall cause pieces of the sky to fall upon them﴾ Hamzah and al-Kisa'i recited, "in yasha' yakhsif aw yusqit" (if He wills, He causes to swallow or causes to fall), with the ya' in all of them, because of the mention of Allah before them. The others recited with the nun in all of them. ﴿Indeed in that﴾ that is, in what you see of the heaven and the earth, ﴿is a sign﴾ indicating Our power over resurrection, ﴿for every servant who turns back﴾ repentant, returning to Allah with his heart.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And We had certainly given David bounty from Us﴾ meaning prophethood and the Book. It was also said: kingship. It was also said: all that he was given of beautiful voice, softening iron, and other things with which he was singled out. ﴿O mountains﴾ that is, and We said: O mountains, ﴿repeat [the praises] with him﴾ that is, glorify [Allah] with him when he glorifies. It was also said: it is tafʻil from al-iyab, which is returning; that is, return with him. Al-Qutaybi said: its origin is from ta'wib in travel, which is to travel the whole day and halt at night, as if he said: repeat the praise with him all day long with glorification. Wahb said: lament with him.

﴿And the birds﴾ is in conjunction with the position of "the mountains," because every vocative noun is in a position of accusative (nasb). It was also said: its meaning is: and We subjected the birds and commanded them to glorify with him. Ya'qub recited "wa'l-tayru" (and the birds) in the nominative, as a response to "the mountains," that is: repeat, you and the birds. When David called out in a direction, the mountains answered him with their echo, and the birds gathered around him from above. The echo of the mountains that people hear today is from that.

It was also said: when David passed among the mountains and glorified Allah, the mountains began to respond to him with glorification, in the manner that he glorified.

It was also said: when David, peace be upon him, became lax, Allah made him hear the glorification of the mountains to energize him. [See: al-Qurtubi, 14/365-366.] ﴿And We made iron soft for him﴾ until the iron was in his hand like wax and dough; he shaped from it whatever he wished without fire or striking with a hammer.

The cause of that, as is related in the reports, was this: when David, peace be upon him, became ruler over the Children of Israel, it was his custom to go out among the people in disguise. When he saw a man he did not know, he approached him, asked him about David, and said: What do you say about David, your ruler, what sort of man is he? They would praise him and speak well of him. Allah then sent to him an angel in the form of a human. When David saw him, he approached him as was his custom and asked him. The angel said: He is an excellent man, were it not for one trait in him. David was alarmed by this and said: What is it, O servant of Allah? He said: He eats and feeds his dependents from the treasury of wealth. He said: Then David was alerted by this and asked Allah to provide him with a means by which he could be independent of the treasury, so he could earn his food and feed his dependents. Allah the Exalted then made iron soft for him and taught him the craft of the coat of mail, and he was the first to make it. [Mentioned by Ibn Kathir, 3/528.] It is said that he used to sell each coat of mail for four thousand dirhams, and would eat from it, feed his dependents, and give charity from it to the poor and needy.

It is also said that he would make one coat of mail each day, which he sold for six thousand dirhams; he spent two thousand of it on himself and his dependents, and gave four thousand in charity to the poor of the Children of Israel. [Narrated by Ibn Kathir, 3/528, and al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur, 6/676, and it is weak.]

The one who makes it is called al-sarrad (السرّاد) and al-zarrad (الزرّاد). He says: measure the rivets in the rings of the mail, meaning do not make the rivets too fine, lest they slip out, nor too thick, lest they break the rings. It is also said that al-sard is the riveting of the ring, and one says "a mail coat that is sarda," meaning its rings are riveted. ﴿And be measured in the weaving﴾ means: make it moderate, according to what is needed.

﴿And work righteousness﴾: he means Dawud and his family.

﴿Indeed, I am Seeing of what you do.﴾

﴿And to Solomon [We subjected] the wind﴾: that is, We subjected the wind to Solomon. Al-Hasan said: He would set out in the morning from Damascus and take his midday rest at Istakhr, with a month's journey between them. It is also said that he would take his midday meal at al-Rayy and his evening meal at Samarqand. [[Refer to what has preceded in the commentary on Surat al-Anbiya'.]]

The scholars of tafsir said: A spring of copper was made to flow for him for three days and their nights, like the flowing of water, and it was in the land of Yemen. He directed the devils in groups, each group bringing out gold, silver, rubies from their mines, and pure pearls from the sea; other groups would pry loose the jewels and stones from their places; and other groups would bring him musk, ambergris, and all kinds of perfume from their sources. [[Narrated by Ibn Majah in al-Iqamah, chapter: What has come concerning prayer in the mosque of Bayt al-Maqdis (1/452), where he said: "And that he would not come to this mosque..." Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 34, verse 14:

﴿Then when We decreed death for him﴾, i.e., for Sulayman.

The people of knowledge (ahl al-'ilm) said: Sulayman, peace be upon him, would seclude himself in Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) for a year or two years, or a month or two months, or less or more than that, and he would bring his food and drink into it. He entered it the time in which he died. The beginning of this was that every morning a tree would sprout in the mihrab of Bayt al-Maqdis, and he would ask it, "What is your name?" It would say, "My name is such-and-such." He would say, "For what purpose are you?" It would say, "For such-and-such." He would then order it to be cut down. If it had sprouted for planting, he would plant it; if it had sprouted for medicine, he would record it, until a carob tree (kharruba) sprouted. He said to it, "What are you?" It said, "The carob." He said, "For what purpose have you sprouted?" It said, "For the ruin of your mosque." Sulayman said, "God would not ruin it while I am alive. You are the one who will bring about my destruction and the ruin of Bayt al-Maqdis!" He uprooted it, planted it in a garden of his, and then said, "O God, conceal my death from the jinn, so that mankind will know that the jinn do not know the unseen." The jinn used to tell mankind that they knew some of the unseen and knew what would happen tomorrow. Then he entered the mihrab and stood praying, leaning on his staff, and he died standing. The mihrab had openings in front of him and behind him. The jinn continued doing those arduous tasks they used to do during his lifetime, looking at him and supposing that he was alive, and they did not object to his being withheld from coming out to the people because of the length of his prayer beforehand. They continued toiling for him after his death for a full year, until the termite ate his staff, whereupon he fell down dead, and they knew of his death. [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 22/75; al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 6/682-683 attributed it to Ibn Abi Hatim. Ibn Kathir said (3/530): "In its being raised (to the Prophet) there is strangeness and abnormality, and the closer view is that it is a mawquf (companion or successor report), and 'Ata' ibn Abi Muslim al-Khurasani has strange reports, and in some of his narrations there is abnormality."]]

Ibn 'Abbas said: The jinn thanked the termite, so they bring it water and clay inside the wood. [[Mentioned by Ibn Kathir (3/531), who said: "This report, and God knows best, is only from what was taken from the scholars of the People of the Book, and it is a mawquf report: nothing from it is affirmed except what agrees with the truth, nothing is denied except what contradicts the truth, and the rest is neither affirmed nor denied."]] Hence His words: ﴿It was only the creature of the earth that showed them his death, eating away his staff﴾, meaning the termite, ﴿eating away his minsanatahu﴾ — meaning his staff. The people of Medina and Abu 'Amr read "minsatahu" without a hamza, while the rest read it with a hamza; both are dialectal forms. Ibn 'Amir reads the hamza as sukun. Its root is from "nasa'tu al-ghanam," meaning I drove the sheep and herded them, and from it: "nasa'a Allah fi ajalihi," meaning God delayed his term.

﴿Then when he fell down﴾, i.e., collapsed to the ground, ﴿the jinn saw clearly﴾, i.e., the jinn knew and became certain, ﴿that had they known the unseen, they would not have remained in the humiliating punishment﴾, i.e., in toil and hardship, subjected to Sulayman while he was dead, which they assumed to be alive. God intended by this to make the jinn know that they do not know the unseen, for they used to suppose that they knew the unseen, due to the predominance of ignorance. Al-Azhari mentioned that the meaning of "tabayyanat al-jinn" is that the jinn became manifest and were revealed to mankind, i.e., their condition became clear, that they do not know the unseen, for they had been deceiving mankind about that. In the reading of Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn 'Abbas: "tabayyanat al-ins" (mankind saw clearly) that if the jinn knew the unseen they would not have remained in the humiliating punishment, i.e., mankind knew and became certain of that.

Ya'qub read "tubayyinat" with a damma on the ta' and a kasra on the ya' [i.e., mankind informed the jinn; it is cited in the impersonal passive form, and "tubayyina" is both intransitive and transitive].

The historians mentioned that Sulayman's age was fifty-three years, the duration of his reign was forty years, and he became king when he was thirteen years old, and he began building Bayt al-Maqdis four years after his reign began.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 34, verses 15–16:**

His statement, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Indeed there was for Sheba, in their dwelling, a sign﴾. Abu Sabra al-Nakha'i narrated from Farwa ibn Musayk al-Ghutayfi, who said: A man said, "O Messenger of Allah, tell me about Saba'. Was he a man, a woman, or a land?" He said: "He was a man from the Arabs, and he had ten sons. Six of them went to the right (tayammana), and four went to the left (tasha'ama). As for those who went right: Kinda, al-Ash'ariyyun, Azd, Muadhhij, Anmar, and Himyar." A man said, "What is Anmar?" He said: "Those among them are Khath'am and Bajila." "As for those who went left: 'Amila, Judham, Lakhm, Ghassan, and Saba'. He is the son of Yashjub ibn Ya'rub ibn Qahtan."

[[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Huruf: 6/8, abridged; and al-Tirmidhi in al-Tafsir: 9/88–89, who said: "This is a gharib hasan hadith." And al-Hakim: 2/224. Al-Suyuti also attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/686–687 to Abd ibn Humayd, al-Bukhari in al-Tarikh, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Mardawayh. See also Majma' al-Zawa'id: 7/94.]]

﴿In their dwelling﴾: Hamza and Hafs read "مَسْكَنِهِمْ" (maskanihim, singular) with a fatha on the kaf. Al-Kisa'i read it with a kasra on the kaf. The others read "مَسَاكِنِهِمْ" (masakinihim, plural). Their dwellings were at Ma'rib in Yemen. ﴿A sign﴾: an indication of Our oneness and Our power. **Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 34, verses 19–20:**

﴿So they said, "Our Lord, lengthen the distance between our journeys."﴾ So make between us and the Levant deserts and wastelands, so that we may ride our mounts across them and take provisions for the road. So God hastened His answer to them. Mujahid said: They were ungrateful for the blessing and tired of comfort.

Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr read *bu'ʻid* (بَعِّدْ) with a shadda (tashdid, doubling of the consonant), from *tab'id* (causing distance). The others read *bā'id* (بَاعِدْ) with an alif. Both are in the form of a supplication and a request. Ya'qub read *Rabbunā* (رَبُّنَا) with a damma on the bā', and *bā'ada* (بَاعَدَ) with a fatha on the ʻayn and the dāl, as a statement of fact, as if they found their nearby journeys too far. They were ungrateful and insolent.

﴿And they wronged themselves﴾ by ingratitude and rebellion.

﴿So We made them into tales﴾ as a lesson for those who came after them, who would speak of their affair and their condition. ﴿And We scattered them completely﴾ We dispersed them in every direction through the lands, a complete dispersal. Al-Sha'bi said: When their settlements were flooded, they scattered through the lands. The Ghassan went to the Levant. The Azd went to Oman. Khuza'a went to Tihama. The family of Khuzayma went to Iraq. The Aws and the Khazraj went to Yathrib. The one among them who came to Medina was ʻAmr ibn ʻAmir, who was the grandfather of the Aws and the Khazraj.

﴿Indeed, in that are signs﴾ lessons and proofs, ﴿for every steadfast one﴾ who restrains himself from the disobedience of God, ﴿grateful﴾ for His blessings. Muqatil said: That means the believer from this community, who is patient under trial and thankful for blessings. Mutarrif said: It is the believer, who gives thanks when he is given, and is patient when he is tested.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And Iblis certainly confirmed his assumption about them﴾. The people of Kufa read *ṣaddaqa* (صَدَّقَ) with tashdid, meaning: he assumed about them an assumption, when he said, "By Your might, I will surely mislead them all" (Sad 82), and "You will not find most of them grateful" (al-A'raf 17). So he confirmed his assumption and made it true by his deed toward them and their following him. The others read it without tashdid, meaning: he was right about them in his assumption about them, that is, concerning the people of Saba'. Mujahid said: concerning all people, except those who obeyed God. ﴿Then they followed him, except for a group of the believers.﴾ Al-Suddi reported from Ibn ʻAbbas: It means all the believers, because the believers did not follow him in the fundamentals of religion. God Almighty has said: "Indeed, over My servants you have no authority" (al-Hijr 42), meaning the believers. It was also said: it is specific to the believers who obey God and do not disobey Him.

Ibn Qutayba said: When Iblis asked for respite and God granted it to him, he said, "I will surely mislead them and lead them astray." He was not certain at the time of this statement that what he said about them would come to pass; he said it as an assumption. When they followed him and obeyed him, what he had assumed about them came true.

Al-Hasan said: He did not draw a sword against them, nor did he strike them with a whip. He only promised them and gave them hopes, and so they were deceived.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 34, verses 37–39:

﴿Neither your wealth nor your children are that which will bring you near to Us in nearness﴾. That is, closeness (qurbā). Al-Akhfash said: "qurbā" is an infinitive noun (ism masdar), as if he had said: "that which will bring you near to Us in bringing near." ﴿Except for one who believes﴾, meaning: but whoever believes, ﴿and does righteous deeds﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: he means that his faith and his deed bring him near to Me. ﴿For them there is a recompense of double for what they did﴾. That is, Allah multiplies their good deeds, so that one good deed is rewarded tenfold up to seven hundred times. Ya'qub recited "jaza'an" in the accusative with tanwin, and "al-ḍi'f" in the nominative, its meaning being: "for them there is the double as a recompense." The majority recited it with the genitive construction (idafa). ﴿And they will be secure in the upper chambers﴾. Hamza recited "fi al-ghurfa" in the singular, while the others recited it in the plural, following His saying: "We will surely settle them in the Garden in chambers (ghuraf)" [al-'Ankabut: 58].

﴿And those who strive﴾, that is, who work, ﴿against Our signs﴾, that is, to nullify Our proof, ﴿seeking to frustrate [them]﴾, that is, who oppose stubbornly, supposing that they can outdo Us and escape Us. ﴿Those will be brought into the punishment.﴾

﴿Say: Indeed, my Lord extends provision to whom He wills of His servants and restricts [it] for him. And whatever you spend of anything, He will replace it﴾. That is, He gives its replacement. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: whatever is spent without extravagance or stinginess, He will replace it.

Al-Kalbi said: whatever charity you give and whatever you spend in good causes, He will replace it for the one who spends, either by hastening it to him in this world or by storing it up for him in the Hereafter.

﴿And He is the best of providers﴾, the best of those who give and provide.

It has been related to us from Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah, the Exalted, said: 'Spend, and I will spend upon you.'" [Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tawhid, chapter: "They wish to change the words of Allah," 13/464; Muslim in Zakat, chapter: Encouraging spending and giving good news to the spender of a replacement, no. 993, 2/690-691; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 6/154.]

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliki informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Isma'il narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Sulayman, namely Ibn Bilal, from Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Muzarrid, from Abu al-Hubahib, from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is not a day on which the servants rise in the morning without two angels descending, one of whom says: 'O Allah, give the spender a replacement,' and the other says: 'O Allah, give the withholder destruction.'" [Narrated by al-Bukhari in Zakat, chapter: the saying of Allah, "As for he who gives and fears Allah and believes in the best reward, We will ease him toward ease," 3/304; Muslim in Zakat, chapter: On the spender and the withholder, no. 1010, 2/700; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 6/155-156.]

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliki informed us, Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Sam'an informed us, Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar al-Rayyani informed us, Humayd ibn Zanjawayh informed us, Ibn Abi Uways informed us, Abd al-Aziz ibn Muhammad informed us, from al-'Ala' ibn Abd al-Rahman, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No charity decreases wealth; Allah does not increase a servant in forgiveness except in honour; and no one humbles himself for Allah except that Allah raises him." [Narrated by Muslim in Birr, Silat and Adab, chapter: Recommendation of pardon and humility, no. 2588, 4/2001; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 6/133.]

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliki informed us, Abu Mansur al-Sam'ani informed us, Abu Ja'far al-Rayyani informed us, Humayd ibn Zanjawayh informed us, Abu al-Rabi' informed us, Abd al-Hamid ibn al-Hasan al-Hilali informed us, Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir informed us, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Every act of kindness is charity, and whatever a man spends on himself and his family is recorded for him as charity, and whatever a man protects his honour with is recorded for him as charity." I said: What is meant by "protects his honour"? He said: "What is given to the poet and to the one who is feared for his tongue. His saying "I said: What is meant" — Abd al-Hamid is saying this to Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir.

Mujahid said: If there is something in one of your hands, let him be moderate, and let him not misinterpret this verse, "whatever you spend of anything, He will replace it," for provision is apportioned; perhaps his provision is little, while he spends like one who is well-off. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 34, verse 40–44:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And the Day He gathers them all﴾ Ya'qub and Hafs recited "yahshuruhum" (with the yaa), while the others recited it with the nun (nahshuruhum). ﴿All﴾ means: these disbelievers. ﴿Then He will say to the angels, "Did these used to worship you?"﴾ in the world. Qatadah said: This is a question of reproach (istifham taqrir), like His saying, the Exalted, to Jesus: ﴿"Did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah?'"﴾ [Maryam: 116]. Then the angels will disown them.

﴿They will say, "Glory be to You"﴾ (tanzih, declaring You far above imperfection), ﴿"You are our Guardian, not them"﴾, meaning: we take You as our ally and we do not take them as allies. ﴿Rather, they used to worship the jinn﴾, meaning: the devils (shayatin). If it is said: they used to worship the angels, so what is the meaning of His saying ﴿they worshipped the jinn﴾? It is said: He intended the devils, who adorned for them the worship of the angels, so they were obeying the devils in worshipping the angels. Thus His saying ﴿worshipped﴾ means: they obeyed the jinn. ﴿Most of them believed in them﴾, meaning: they affirmed the devils as true.

Then Allah says: ﴿So today none of you has power to benefit or harm another﴾ through intercession (shafa'ah) or through punishment (ʿadhab), meaning that they are powerless; there is no benefit with them and no harm. ﴿And We will say to those who did wrong, "Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny."﴾

﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them, they say, "This is nothing but a man who wants to turn you away from what your fathers used to worship,"﴾ meaning Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿And they say, "This is nothing but a fabricated lie,"﴾ meaning the Qur'an. ﴿And those who disbelieved said of the truth when it came to them, "This is nothing but obvious magic,"﴾ meaning: clear.

﴿And We did not give them﴾ meaning: these polytheists, ﴿any books which they study﴾ read, ﴿nor did We send to them before you any warner﴾, meaning: no prophet came to the Arabs before you, and no book was revealed to them.

**And they had disbelieved in it before** — i.e., in the Qur'an; and it is said: in Muhammad (ﷺ) — **before they witnessed the punishment and the terrors of the Resurrection. And they hurl (speculation) about the unseen from a distant place.** Mujahid said: they throw at Muhammad (ﷺ) accusations based on conjecture, not certainty, and these are their sayings: "a sorcerer," "a poet," and "a soothsayer." The meaning of *al-ghayb* (the unseen) here is conjecture, because its knowledge has been hidden from them (*ghába*). The "distant place" refers to their distance from knowledge of what they are saying. The meaning is: they hurl at Muhammad (ﷺ) what they do not know, from a place where they have no knowledge. Qatadah said: they cast stones by conjecture, saying, "There is no resurrection, no Paradise, and no Hellfire."

**And a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire** — i.e., faith, repentance, and returning to the world. It is also said: the bounties of the world and its splendor. **As was done with their counterparts** — i.e., with their likes and those who were in a similar state to theirs among the disbelievers — **before** them. That is, faith and repentance were not accepted from them at the time of despair. **Indeed they were in doubt** — concerning the Resurrection and the descent of punishment upon them — **a disquieting doubt**, one that caused them unease and suspicion.
